therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Dual inhibition of protein kinase C and MEK kinases
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Disruption of oncogenic signaling pathways in uveal melanoma
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adult patients with metastatic uveal melanoma
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Phase Ib: Dose limiting toxicities; Phase II: Progression free survival

results.effect_size: Median PFS ranged from 3.1 to 4.0 weeks across dose cohorts
results.target_engagement_evidence: Pharmacokinetic data showed dose-proportional exposure for both compounds
subgroup_findings: No complete or partial responses observed in any dose cohort
Best response was stable disease across all cohorts
safety_signals: Multiple dose-limiting toxicities including diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, fatigue
High incidence of serious adverse events across dose levels
Dermatitis acneiform observed as DLT at 200mg AEB071 + 45mg MEK162

dose_info.dose: AEB071: 150-400 mg BID; MEK162: 30-45 mg BID
dose_info.max_tolerated_dose: Not determined - study terminated before MTD establishment
dose_info.dose_modifications: Study terminated prior to MTD determination due to enrollment halt

context.duration: up to 18 months from Last Patient First Visit
context.investigator_commentary: The trial was terminated for scientific reasons. Due to an enrollment halt, the Phase II part of the study was not conducted. The sponsor decided to permanently stop recruitment for the study prior to MTD determination.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: PKC inhibition was hypothesized to enhance MEK inhibition through complementary pathway blockade
modulation_entries.citation: Due to an enrollment halt, the Phase II part of the study was not conducted. The sponsor decided to permanently stop recruitment for the study prior to MTD determination.
